sections.label: Singapore Budget support packages
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister presented a $5.6 billion support package on 18 February and a $48 billion second package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If you look at Singapore on 18 February, the Deputy Prime Minister presented his Budget speech with a support package of $5.6 billion dollars – very substantive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: At that time, there were 800 confirmed cases outside China.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There was a second package presented by the Deputy Prime Minister – this time, $48 billion.

sections.label: Third package for Singaporeans
sections.summary: On 6 April, the Deputy Prime Minister presented the third package to help Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Yesterday, 6 April, the Deputy Prime Minister presented the third package to help Singaporeans.

sections.label: Three Budgets committed funds
sections.summary: Three Budgets between 18 February and 6 April committed close to $60 billion, 12% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And the response to all of this, to such a serious shock, has to try and meet the challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, we first had the three Budgets between 18 February and 6 April, close to $60 billion committed – 12% of our GDP.

sections.label: Blaisdell Supreme Court judgment
sections.summary: In the 1934 Blaisdell case, the court held the state has a duty to safeguard vital interests and power to intervene.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This being America, the laws were challenged and went up to the Supreme Court, ended up in a famous case in 1934, Blaisdell, where the court gave a long judgment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But, if I can summarise into two points: the state has a duty to safeguard vital interests of its people; the state has the power to intervene, to safeguard the economic structure upon which the good of all depends.

sections.label: US examples and current situation
sections.summary: Examples were chosen from the US, and the current situation appears worse than the Global Financial Crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I have deliberately chosen examples from the US because it is often seen as the ultimate capitalist free-market economy, other than possibly Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, the situation we have today, at this stage, appears to be worse than the Global Financial Crisis.

sections.label: Principles for retroactive legislation
sections.summary: Principles for retroactive legislation include vital interests at stake, state intervention, and reasonable steps of limited duration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The principles applicable for such retroactive legislation: one, the vital interests of the people are at stake, a significant part of the economy is at stake.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Third, the state can intervene to use reasonable means to safeguard the economic structure for common good.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And to this end, four, the state can take reasonable steps generally of limited duration.

sections.label: Construction workforce shortage and shrinkage
sections.summary: SCAL said some sites face up to 40% workforce shortage, and construction shrank 4.3% in the first quarter and nearly 23% from the previous quarter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Singapore Contractor Association Limited (SCAL) said some sites are experiencing up to 40% shortage in workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The construction sector has shrank 4.3% in the first quarter of this year and nearly 23% as compared to the previous quarter.

sections.label: Bill validity and extension power
sections.summary: The Bill will first be valid for six months, and the Minister can extend it up to a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In the first instance, the Bill will be valid for six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Minister will be given power to extend it, up to a year.

sections.label: Tenant relief conditions and protections
sections.summary: A tenant must show inability to pay rent during the prescribed period caused materially by a COVID-19 event, and then the lease cannot be terminated and legal proceedings cannot start.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: A tenant who seeks relief must show that he is unable to pay rent during the prescribed period and that the inability to pay is to a material extent caused by a COVID-19 event.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If he can show, that then the lease or licence cannot be terminated on the basis that rent has not been paid; and legal proceedings cannot be commenced against tenants on the basis that rent has not been paid.

sections.label: Rental relief and sector rental value
sections.summary: Relief requires inability to pay rent materially caused by COVID-19, and industrial and commercial rental value was about $21 billion in 2018, with SME rentals about $14 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, relief is only available where there is an inability to pay rent; and that inability to pay rent is, to a material extent, caused by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This intervention is substantial because the total value of rental in our industrial and commercial sectors is estimated in 2018 – when figures are available – to be at about $21 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Of that, if you look at the SMEs' rentals, that is about $14 billion – covers both services and manufacturing.

sections.label: SME share of employment
sections.summary: SMEs accounted for 72% of employment in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: SMEs accounted for 72% of employment in Singapore.

sections.label: Construction materials disruption and payment drops
sections.summary: Disruption affected precast, prefabricated, prefinished and volumetric construction materials from Malaysia, and progress payments dropped between 5% and 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: More recently, disruption of precast and prefabricated, prefinished, volumetric construction materials, other types of materials coming into Singapore from Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I talked about SCAL saying sites are experiencing up to 40% shortage in workforce and drop in progress payments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Progress payments have dropped anywhere between 5% and 20%, and it will probably get worse.

sections.label: Construction contracts awarded value
sections.summary: The total value of construction contracts awarded last year in Singapore was $33 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The total value of construction contracts awarded last year in Singapore amounted to $33 billion.

sections.label: Event deposits and COVID-19
sections.summary: Contracts for events like wedding banquets and conferences, including catering and accommodation, must restore or not forfeit deposits if events from 1 February 2020 could not proceed due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: For example, contracts to hold wedding banquets, business meetings, conferences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: They include catering, provision of other goods or services for such events and certain contracts for accommodation, entertainment, tourism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If the event was scheduled to be held on or after 1 February 2020 and could not proceed due to a COVID-19 event, any deposits forfeited must be restored as if they had not been forfeited.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Deposits that have not yet been forfeited must also not be forfeited.

sections.label: Parts 4 and 5 provisions
sections.summary: Clause 27 deals with alternative arrangements for meetings usually held in person, and clause 28 provides for Court proceedings by remote means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Minister Shanmugam, just take pause on the party.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: I will now deal with Parts 4 and 5 of the Bill which introduce two provisions – clause 27, which deals with alternative arrangements for meetings which are usually required to be held in person – the attendance of the shareholders, for example, in person at an AGM; and also clause 28 which provides for the conduct of Court proceedings by remote means.

sections.label: Large corporates deferring AGMs
sections.summary: DBS Group Holdings, OCBC and Great Eastern, large corporates with over a thousand shareholders, had to defer their AGMs pending the Bill's passing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, DBS Group Holdings, OCBC and Great Eastern, three examples of large corporates where ordinarily more than a thousand shareholders would attend the meetings – and there are other companies – have had to defer their AGMs, pending the passing of this Bill.

sections.label: Meeting flexibility and safe distancing
sections.summary: Inability to hold meetings caused uncertainty and disruption, so Part 4 allows flexibility for meetings complying with safe distancing while maintaining propriety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, across a range of sectors and in the financial markets, the inability to hold meetings has led to a significant degree of uncertainty and disruption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Hence, Part 4 of this Bill seeks to introduce and allow some flexibility for the conduct of meetings to be held in compliance with the necessary safe distancing measures, while at the same time, maintaining propriety in the conduct of these meetings.

sections.label: Minister may prescribe arrangements
sections.summary: Under clause 27, the Minister for Law may prescribe by order any alternative meeting arrangement he considers necessary or desirable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under clause 27, the Minister for Law may prescribe, by order, any alternative meeting arrangement he considers necessary or desirable for that meeting or class of meetings to take place.

sections.label: Clause 27 meeting options
sections.summary: Clause 27(2) prescribes a suite of options for the Minister to prescribe for different meeting types, and clause 27 applies retrospectively from 27 March.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: There is not a one-size-fits-all approach, which is why clause 27(2) prescribes a suite of options available to the Minister to prescribe, as may be appropriate, from one type of meeting to another.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: I should highlight to Members that clause 27, like some other parts of this Bill, applies retrospectively, from 27 March, the date of MOH’s Safe-Distancing Regulations.

sections.label: Joint press release on Bill
sections.summary: MinLaw and MOH issued a joint press release on 31 March announcing the proposed provisions and the intention for retrospective application from 27 March.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In the period leading up to the publication of this Bill, MinLaw and MOH issued a joint press release on 31 March announcing these proposed legislative provisions so that the market and its users were clear, and also making clear that the intention was for this Bill to apply retrospectively from 27 March.

sections.label: Remote giving of evidence
sections.summary: Accused persons in Singapore and specified categories of witnesses from abroad can give evidence remotely by video or television link in Court proceedings, subject to conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Subject to conditions which I will outline, accused persons in Singapore and specified categories of witnesses from abroad can give evidence remotely, either by video or television link, in any Court proceedings.

sections.label: Ceasing clause 28 application
sections.summary: The measures apply only during the specified period, allowing the Minister for Law to declare clause 28 cease to apply to Court or Syariah Court proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, the measures will only apply during the specified period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These allow the Minister for Law, in consultation with the Chief Justice or the Minister in charge of Muslim Affairs, to declare that clause 28 would cease to apply to any Court or Syariah Court proceedings, respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These provisions will ensure that commerce and the administration of justice do not grind to a complete halt, even as we observe the circuit breaker measures which the Government has implemented.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Owners of such properties are granted a property tax rebate of 30%, 60% or 100%, depending on the nature of the property, for 2020.

sections.label: 2020 property tax rebate coverage
sections.summary: The 2020 property tax rebate will cover about 135,000 property tax accounts, including 33,000 accounts for about 360 retail malls.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In total, the 2020 property tax rebate will cover about 135,000 property tax accounts, including 33,000 property tax accounts for about 360 retail malls.

sections.label: Passing on property tax rebate
sections.summary: The Bill requires a property owner to pass on the full amount of property tax rebate attributable to a rented property to his tenant in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Specifically, the Bill requires a property owner to pass on the full amount of property tax rebate attributable to a rented property to his tenant, in a timely manner.

sections.label: Property tax rebate dispute deadline
sections.summary: Any dispute over this year's property tax rebate transfer must be brought to the Panel by 31 December 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Any dispute relating to the transfer of the property tax rebate granted this year must be brought to the Panel by 31 December 2021.

sections.label: Multi-Ministry Taskforce measures details
sections.summary: The Multi-Ministry Taskforce shared measures including full home-based learning, closing most workplaces, prohibiting social gatherings and urging Singaporeans to stay home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: On the same day, the Multi-Ministry Taskforce shared the details of these measures, which include moving towards full home-based learning for our schools, closing most physical workplace and other premises, prohibiting social gatherings and urging Singaporeans to stay home and not to go out unnecessarily.

sections.label: Daily new cases crossed 100
sections.summary: The daily number of new cases crossed the 100 mark two days ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The daily number of new cases crossed the 100 mark two days ago.

sections.label: COVID-19 Temporary Measures Bill provisions
sections.summary: The COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Bill gives the Minister for Health power to close premises while allowing essential services to remain open.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To effect our plans, we have included provisions in the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Bill to provide the legal basis to enforce the enhanced safe distancing measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Bill provides the Minister for Health the power to close premises, such as workplaces, schools, recreational facilities and places of worship, to minimise interactions and reduce the risk of COVID-19 transmission; while allowing premises that provide essential services or are in selected economic sectors which are critical to our local and global supply chains to remain open so that services vital to Singapore’s security and to Singaporeans’ daily living can continue to be provided.

sections.label: Social gatherings disallowed
sections.summary: Events and mass gatherings were earlier deferred or cancelled, and social gatherings of any size in private and public places will now be disallowed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, we had earlier required certain events and mass gatherings to be deferred or cancelled.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will now also disallow social gatherings of any size in both private and public places.

sections.label: Penalties for safe distancing offences
sections.summary: First-time offenders face a fine up to $10,000, up to six months' imprisonment, or both, with higher penalties for repeat offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For first-time offenders, the penalty is a fine of up to $10,000, or imprisonment of up to six months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For second or subsequent offences, the penalty is a fine of up to $20,000, or imprisonment of up to 12 months, or both.

sections.label: Circuit breaker until 4 May
sections.summary: The circuit breaker will be imposed until 4 May.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The circuit breaker will be imposed until 4 May.

sections.label: Moratorium on five kinds of actions
sections.summary: Clauses 5(2), 5(3) and 6(2) impose a moratorium over five kinds of actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The core provisions of this part of the Bill can essentially be found in clauses 5(2), 5(3) and 6(2).

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These provisions impose a moratorium over five kinds of actions: Court and insolvency proceedings, enforcement of judgments and arbitration decisions, the enforcement of certain types of security, the calling on a performance bond pursuant to a construction contract, and the termination of leases of non-residential premises.

sections.label: Higher thresholds for bankruptcy and insolvency
sections.summary: Clause 20 raises the bankruptcy threshold to $60,000 and clause 21 raises the insolvency threshold to $100,000, both extending statutory demand periods to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For instance, clause 20 raises the monetary threshold for bankruptcy applications from $15,000 to $60,000 and increases the time period to satisfy or set aside a statutory demand from the current 21 days to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For businesses, clause 21 increases the monetary threshold for insolvency from $10,000 to $100,000 and similarly extends the time period to satisfy or set aside statutory demands to six months.

sections.label: Court orders for live video evidence
sections.summary: Clause 28(1) empowers the court to order an accused person or witness to give evidence by live video or live television link.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 28(1) empowers the court to make orders to require an accused person or witness to give evidence in any court proceedings by a live video or live television link.

sections.label: Assessors panel workload and timely decisions
sections.summary: A question asks if the Minister intends measures to ensure the panel of Assessors is not overwhelmed and can still decide justly and timely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While the assessment process is undoubtedly intended to be a fast and efficient one, given the existing universe of contracts and the potential number and complexity of disputes, I would like to ask if the Minister intends to put in place measures to ensure that the panel of Assessors are not overwhelmed and are yet still able to arrive at just decisions in a timely manner.

sections.label: Assessors' power over partial payments
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Assessors' power to achieve a just and equitable outcome includes ordering partial payments or using a tenant's security deposit to offset rental arrears.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Does the Assessors' power to achieve a just and equitable outcome include the power to determine that partial payments be made or that a tenant's security deposit may be used to offset rental arrears.

sections.label: Online portal for dispute assessments
sections.summary: Asks whether the Minister would consider digital measures such as an online portal for requesting assessments, uploading documents and receiving determinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Would the Minister consider putting in place digital measures to make the process as simple and straightforward as possible, such as through the use of an online portal to allow parties to request for assessments, upload documents and even receive determinations for appropriate disputes?

sections.label: Guidance after Bill ceases
sections.summary: Asks whether the Minister is looking into guidance, such as asking contracting parties to negotiate instalment payments for liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, once the Bill ceases to have effect and this dam is removed, the combined obligations could be quite harsh.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I wish to ask if the Minister is looking into providing guidance, such as asking contracting parties to use this period to negotiate with those they have contracted with, to be able to pay off their liabilities in instalments.

sections.label: Temporary relief for scheduled contracts
sections.summary: Speech covers temporary measures in the Bill giving relief from actions for inability to perform scheduled contracts caused by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: My speech today will touch on the temporary measures in the Bill to provide relief from actions for inability to perform scheduled contracts, as outlined in the Schedule of the Bill, caused by COVID-19 on or after 1 February 2020 for contracts entered into before 25 March 2020.

sections.label: Protection for tenants unable to pay rent
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to protect individual or industrial tenants from damages, forfeited deposits, litigation or insolvency for inability to pay rent due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: On the delay of rental payments, the Bill seeks to protect individual or industrial tenants from having to pay damages or forfeit deposits, or face lengthy litigation or possible insolvency for inability to pay rent due to the COVID-19 situation, which they have no control over.

sections.label: Rent accrues after relief period
sections.summary: For tenants who sought temporary relief, rent continues to accrue and remains payable after the six months' temporary relief period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For the tenants who have sought such temporary relief, rent will continue to accrue and remains payable after the six months' temporary relief period.

sections.label: Contractor not liable for liquidated damages
sections.summary: The contractor will not be liable for liquidated damages, delays and non-supply of goods arising from the COVID-19 event.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The contractor will not be liable for liquidated damages, delays and non-supply of goods arising from the COVID-19 event.

sections.label: HDB flat sale handover
sections.summary: Sellers of HDB flats must hand over flats they live in by an agreed date, and renovation works must stop from today to 4 May.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Sellers of HDB flats, for example, have to hand over flats that they currently live in by an agreed date to the new owner for the completion of the sale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But renovation works have and should stop from now, from today to 4 May.

sections.label: Property tax rebate for tenants
sections.summary: The Supplementary Budget grants enhanced property tax rebate for 2020, and the Bill makes it a legal obligation for landlords to pass rebates to tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Supplementary Budget grants enhanced rebate for the property tax payable for the period of 1 January 2020 to 31 December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the unexpected impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the businesses, I am glad that the Bill seeks to make it a legal obligation to ensure that landlords pass on the benefits of the enhanced property tax rebates to tenants, as these rebates were meant for the tenants.

sections.label: Landlord re-entry and forfeiture
sections.summary: Clause 5 provides that a landlord cannot exercise re-entry or forfeiture rights under a scheduled non-residential lease or licence, or similar rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the proposed Bill provides that a landlord cannot exercise his right of re-entry or forfeiture under a scheduled contract, being a lease or licence of a non-residential immovable property, and the landlord cannot the exercise any other right that has a similar outcome.

sections.label: MAS on banks' contractual rights
sections.summary: MAS stated banks' contractual rights are unaffected except commencing legal action for loan default, and banks can still charge fees and interest for late or non-payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In the response from MAS to the Bill, MAS stated that the contractual rights of banks are not affected, other than the right to commence legal action for a default on a loan covered under the proposed Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Banks’ contractual right to charge fees and interest for non-payment or late payment of loan obligations due is unaffected, meaning to say banks can continue to charge fees and interest for late payment or non-payment of the loan obligations.

sections.label: Mandatory passing of property tax remission
sections.summary: Clause 29 makes it mandatory for landlords to pass property tax remission benefits to tenants, and the Malaysian Movement Control Order affected workers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I wish to express my support for clause 29 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This clause 29 makes it mandatory for a landlord to pass on the benefit of the property tax remission to the tenant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Many tenants that I speak to were very unhappy that they have not seen any benefit being passed on to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Many of them share that their landlords have been stalling and giving excuses for not passing on the tax remission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: To the other landlords who are still thinking about it, this Bill makes that decision non-negotiable and this is good for the landlord.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The tenant survives, continues to pay the rental to the landlord and the landlord continues to get his steady stream of rental income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Malaysian Government imposed a Movement Control Order from 18 to 31 March, with a further extension to 14 April, as a measure to contain the spread of COVID-19 has affected many of our friends from across the Causeway who are working in Singapore.

sections.label: Deterring service buyers
sections.summary: The Bill aims to deter service buyers from acting high-handedly and imposing liquidated damages for shortfalls due to manpower shortage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With this Bill, I hope that firstly, service buyers will be deterred from acting in a high-handed manner and will not be able to impose liquidated damages for any shortfall in service standards due to manpower shortage.

sections.label: Cleaning workforce reduction request
sections.summary: A cleaning company was asked to cut its workforce from 100 to eight cleaners within a very short time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: One cleaning company shared with the Union that his company was asked to reduce his cleaning workforce by 92% from a workforce of 100 to only eight cleaners within a very short frame of time.

sections.label: Service buyers cutting contract fees
sections.summary: A Member calls the unilateral decision unfair and cites service buyers seeking 10% to 20% contract fee cuts due to wage subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Such unilateral decision is unfair, and I would like to suggest for the Bill to look into such issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I have also received feedback from unionised companies about their service buyers wanting to reduce their contract fees by 10% to 20%, simply because the service buyers perceived that their service providers would be able to do so due to the wage subsidies they would be receiving from the Enhanced Jobs Support Scheme.

sections.label: Call for win-win solutions
sections.summary: The Member hopes the Bill compels service buyers to speak with providers and work out a win-win solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While it is understandable that service buyers who are affected by the COVID-19 situation are finding ways to cut costs, I hope this Bill will compel service buyers to speak to their service providers and be reasonable to work out a win-win solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I believe that it will be our spirit of solidarity, peppered with a lot of empathy and compassion that will pull us through this crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In English): Together with the support of our Government, let us all do our part to support our businesses and workers and we shall overcome as SGUnited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am confident that workers, employers and Government will stand united and ready to fight this virus.

sections.label: Relief tenure and sunset clause
sections.summary: The Bill states a six-month relief tenure extendable by the Minister and a sunset clause after one year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Bill mentioned the relief tenure as six months in the first instance; which can be extended by the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And there is also sunset clause that the Bill will cease to have effect after one year.

sections.label: Assessors for dispute determination
sections.summary: The Law Minister appointed 100 Assessors to assess and determine disputes fairly and objectively, with no recourse for appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the event of disputes, I understand that the Law Minister have appointed a pool of 100 Assessors to assess and determine disputes in a fair and objective manner; with no recourse for appeal.

sections.label: Chain effect of relief
sections.summary: Relief for one party could worsen the other's cash flow, with a possible chain effect, though impact is limited to a specific period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: When one party gets the relief or protection, the other party’s financial or cash flow situation could become more dire because of the non-collection rental from tenants, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We could potentially see a chain effect if each party seeks the relief upstream; although the overall impact across the economy would be limited as this relief measures only apply to a specific period of non-performance after 1 February 2020 and does not apply to contracts entered on or after 25 March 2020.

sections.label: Asset-backed loans and relief
sections.summary: The speaker notes the Bill focuses on asset-backed loans and hopes Assessors can direct loan restructuring and prohibit late payment interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I detect the careful calibration of the measures here in the Bill, primarily focusing on financing that are backed with security, such as loans secured against property or plant, machinery and other equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These asset-back loans tend to be better credit and hence a lower potential loan loss ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Also, there will be follow-on economic ramifications if such assets like machinery and equipment are being seized, as it may result in further disruption to the business ecosystem which works on interdependency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I hope that the Assessors beside determining the relief could also direct a process to restructure the loan that is to mutual benefit of both parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I hope there is also prohibition for late payment interest or charges in this Bill.

sections.label: Chope restaurant survey findings
sections.summary: A Chope survey found 78% of restaurants could not last beyond six months, 80% are cutting staff and a third imposed compulsory leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A survey conducted by Chope, an online dining-reservation booking platform, found that 78% of the restaurants involved were not prepared to last longer than six months if the current situation does not improve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Eighty percent are reducing staff to cut costs and about one-third have asked their full-time staff to take compulsory leave.

sections.label: Shops' sales reduction
sections.summary: Some shops have seen sales fall by up to 90%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Some of these shops have seen a reduction in their sales of up to 90%.

sections.label: SMEs' economic contribution
sections.summary: SMEs account for over 65% of Singapore's employment and contribute almost $200 billion, or 49%, to the economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: SMEs play a very important role in our economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They account for over 65% of Singapore's employment and contribute almost $200 billion, or 49%, to our economy.

sections.label: Tenant protection and rent deferment
sections.summary: The Bill protects commercial tenants from court and insolvency proceedings and lease termination for six months but does not regulate rent repayment or late payment interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: That would be very helpful to tenants, especially the SMEs, micro SMEs and individual proprietors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This Bill also seeks to protect, amongst others, commercial tenants from court and insolvency proceedings and termination of leases for a period of six months from the commencement of the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, I would like to request for the Ministry to take a more comprehensive and long-term view of the impact of these measures on the entire economic value chain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This Bill whilst easing the cash flow of tenants that choose to defer the rent payment, does not go further to regulate the repayment of the six-month rent and the interest on late payment.

sections.label: Legislating rent repayment terms
sections.summary: The Bill only defers the issue, so it should legislate repayment terms and interest after the rent deferment period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The purpose of the Bill is to provide tenants time and space so that their businesses could recover from the COVID-19 situation but the Bill as it stands would only defer the issue further down the road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, to better protect the tenants, the Bill should also legislate the repayment terms upon the expiry of the rent deferment period and the interest charged.

sections.label: Deferment period for tenants
sections.summary: The speaker appeals for a shorter deferment period, such as three months with extension, to balance risks between landlords and tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: They face collapse of their businesses with employees losing their jobs and them losing their properties to the banks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hence, in fairness, I appeal to the Ministry for this deferment measure to be implemented for a shorter period such as three months with extension, as determined by the Minister so that risks are more balanced out between landlords and tenants.

sections.label: SPH REIT retail investors
sections.summary: SPH REIT reported a 78.7% year-on-year decline in distribution per unit despite a 12.2% rise in Income Available for Distribution, affecting over 200,000 retail investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As an example, SPH REIT had announced a 78.7% year-on-year decline in its distribution per unit despite a 12.2% increase in Income Available for Distribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: More than 200,000 retail investors in S-REIT units valued at more than S$15 billion, are our ordinary man in the street – retirees, employees, homemakers and even students.

sections.label: Expanding relief to real estate companies
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Minister expands Temporary Relief from Actions for Inability to Perform Scheduled Contracts to all real estate companies, excluding residential, and all loan types.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is therefore important, that we balance the needs of this group of people even as we help our tenants weather through this difficult time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We hope the Minister would consider expanding the Temporary Relief from Actions for Inability to Perform Scheduled Contracts to include all real estate companies, excluding residential and for all loan types, to mitigate the potential implications as mentioned above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We hope that the Minister further consider these implications and strike a balance in mitigating the challenges that all parties are currently facing.

sections.label: Fairness in COVID-19 Bill
sections.summary: The Bill embeds fairness as COVID-19 affects contractual performance, with targeted protection from legal action providing cash flow relief for impacted sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The element of fairness is embedded in this Bill as COVID-19 is an unexpected event that affects the ability of businesses and individuals to perform contractual obligations, and there is targeted protection from legal action providing cash flow relief for impacted sectors.

sections.label: No termination for non-payment
sections.summary: For non-residential leases or licences, the Bill ensures no termination where non-payment of rent is due to a COVID-19 event.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As mentioned previously, by hon Member of Parliament, Mr Chong Kee Hiong, in the case of leases or licences for non-residential property, this Bill ensures no termination of leased licence where non-payment of rent is due to a COVID-19 event.

sections.label: Moral hazard in deferred payments
sections.summary: The speaker says deferred payment measures should not lead to moral hazard or negative externality issues such as delayed payments or non-performing bank loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In addition, we should also ensure that these measures for deferred payment for six months do not lead to a moral hazard or negative externality issues, where tenants who are already facing trouble take the opportunity to delay payments or lead to non-performing bank loans, causing potential issues, in the future, in the banking system.

sections.label: Booking peak period contracts
sections.summary: Events peak period means venues and services are booked far in advance, but new regulations only apply to contracts entered into before 25 March.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Because this is the peak period for events, venues and services often have to be booked far in advance, sometimes as early as the first half of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, the new regulations only apply to contracts entered into before 25 March.

sections.label: Commercial landlords property tax rebates
sections.summary: It is now mandated by law for commercial landlords to pass property tax rebates to tenants in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Next, on ensuring commercial landlords pass property tax rebates to tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am relieved to note that it is now mandated by law for commercial landlords to pass property tax rebates on to tenants and in a timely manner.

sections.label: Landlord circumvention and fine concerns
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned landlords may circumvent the law with token sums or long instalments, and that the $5,000 fine is low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am concerned that without specifications, landlords may circumvent this with a token sum or long drawn out instalment period that serves little practical purpose to help the tenant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I also note that the fine of $5,000 on property owners guilty of the offence is quite low and the deterrent effect may be too insignificant.

sections.label: Percentage of annual rent
sections.summary: In practice, this is usually about 12% of annual rent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In practice, this is usually about 12% of annual rent.

sections.label: Revised bankruptcy limits
sections.summary: The revised limits of bankruptcy applied to individuals and businesses are timely and should help them during the six-month period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The revised limits of bankruptcy applied to individuals and businesses are timely and should help them during the six-month period.

sections.label: Clause 5 lease moratorium
sections.summary: Clause 5 of the Bill provides a moratorium for the termination of a lease or licence of property for non-payment of rent for six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Bill provides a moratorium for the termination of a lease or licence of property for non-payment of rent for the prescribed period of six months.

sections.label: Tenant's rent and recovery
sections.summary: A tenant's monthly rental is $8,000, and she said six months would accumulate $48,000 in rent, which she is unlikely to pay off in six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Her current monthly rental is $8,000 and she told me that at the end of six months, she would have accumulated $48,000 in rent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Even if she has some relief from paying the rent for these six months, it is unlikely that her business will have fully recovered by that time and she is unlikely to be able to pay off this $48,000 in six months' time.

sections.label: German Bill and rent non-payment
sections.summary: Under the German Bill, landlords may not terminate lease agreements solely because a tenant failed to pay rent from 1 April 2020 to 30 June 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the German Bill, landlords may not terminate lease agreements solely on the grounds that a tenant failed to pay its rent during the period from 1 April 2020 to 30 June 2020.

sections.label: Freelancer relief and remote witnesses
sections.summary: A question asks about relief for freelancers from business contracts including long-term vehicle leases, and clause 28(2)(b)(ii) requires parties' consent for factual witnesses giving evidence remotely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share if there are plans to provide some relief for freelancers from their business contracts, including obligations under long-term vehicle leases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Clause 28(2)(b)(ii) provides that parties' consent must be given for a factual witness to give evidence through remote communication technology.

sections.label: Court oversight of withholding consent
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Court would oversee the reasonableness of a party withholding consent to remote communication technology for factual witnesses, and how that oversight would be exercised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify if the Court would have oversight over the reasonableness of a party withholding consent to the use of remote communication technology for factual witnesses in appropriate cases?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If so, can the Minister share how the oversight will be exercised?

sections.label: Clause 5 temporary relief conditions
sections.summary: Clause 5 stipulates three conditions for temporary relief from contractual consequences, and clarification is sought on the phrase "unable to perform an obligation".

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Clause 5, in my personal view, is the critical provision in this Bill, as it stipulates three conditions pursuant to which temporary relief from contractual consequences may be obtained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I seek clarification on the phrase “unable to perform an obligation”.

sections.label: Clause 5(1)(b) COVID-19 event
sections.summary: Clause 5(1)(b) of the Bill deals with the second condition, "inability to a material extent caused by a COVID-19 event".

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Next, I turn to clause 5(1)(b) of the Bill which deals with the second condition – “inability to a material extent caused by a COVID-19 event”.

sections.label: Clause 6 performance bond
sections.summary: Speaker supports clause 6, which prevents calling on a performance bond for a subject inability caused by a COVID-19 event.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I now turn to clause 6 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I support the intention behind the clause which is to prevent the owner or developer under a contract to call on a performance bond in relation to a “subject inability”, which is defined as the inability to a material extent caused by a COVID-19 event.

sections.label: Defaulting parties Court arbitration
sections.summary: The temporary relief measures contemplate that defaulting parties cannot be subject to Court proceedings or arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As mentioned by the hon Minister, as part of the temporary relief measures, it is contemplated that defaulting parties cannot be subject of Court proceedings as well as arbitration.

sections.label: Extending schedule to trading contracts
sections.summary: Extending the schedule to trading contracts could let international companies commence international arbitration under the IAA, escaping the provision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Should the Minister extend the schedule to cover trading contracts, for example, there could be international companies involved which means that these companies could possibly commence international arbitration which is governed by the International Arbitration Act (IAA), thereby escaping this provision.

sections.label: Remote meetings and Wills witnesses
sections.summary: The Bill provides for remote general meetings and Court proceedings, and a Guardian article said the UK Ministry of Justice is looking at relaxing Wills witness rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill contains provisions for holding of general meetings of companies and Court proceedings using remote communication technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I read a Guardian article dated 31 March 2020 in which it was stated that the UK Ministry of Justice is looking at temporarily relaxing the rules on two witnesses required under the Wills Act as UK self-isolates.

sections.label: Digitising Wills recommendation
sections.summary: If the COVID-19 event extends longer, the speaker recommends the Minister for Law consider looking into digitising Wills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the event the COVID-19 event extends to a longer period of time – and, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I am touching wood at this point in time – I recommend that the Minister for Law consider looking into digitising Wills.

sections.label: Lease termination offence and buffer
sections.summary: The Bill makes it an offence to terminate a lease, repossess premises or start insolvency proceedings against a tenant, creating a buffer period while contractual obligations remain enforceable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Everyone is well aware of the cash flow crisis that operators in the tourism, events and F&B sectors are facing with the collapse in demand and issues to supply chain disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That, under this Bill, it is now an offence to terminate a lease, repossess premises and/or start insolvency proceedings against a tenant service to create a buffer period, allowing them hope of a platform from which to rebuild their business when life returns to normalcy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The other objective of the Bill is the reciprocal corresponding assurance that contractual obligations are still enforceable, that its rights are not extinguished, just temporarily placed on hold.

sections.label: Business continuity and alternative meetings
sections.summary: The Bill provides legally recognised alternative meeting arrangements compliant with safe distancing regulations, and calls on businesses to adopt digital solutions supported by the Supplementary Budget 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us work together to ensure business continuity amist these uncertain times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill also provide for alternative meeting arrangements to be recognised legally, to be compliant with the safe distancing regulations that came into force on 27 March 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: New regulations to put greater distance between co-workers to minimise the spread of COVID-19 have spurred more businesses to adopt a whole suite of digital solutions from video conferencing, workflow management to online ordering and inventory management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Now that the Supplementary Budget 2020 has provided for expanded pre-approved digital solutions to the digital project management system and other grants to support businesses in the required adoptions in response to COVID-19, I call on businesses to please explore the programmes available and I am sure the implementation of these solutions will prove to provide long-term value for companies rather than just short-term solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the first instance, with nearly 200,000 SMEs in Singapore, the volume of contracts signed is indeed voluminous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While not all contracts are expected to be in dispute, it is imperative that the Ministry carefully put in place measures to select and appoint the right Assessors given that there is no appeal mechanism provided for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such Assessors must also be careful to understand and avoid conflicts of interests and buyers whether perceived, potential or actual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such Assessors should also have been placed teleconferencing capabilities to avoid any face-to-face interactions with those raising disputes.

sections.label: Security agencies excluded from relief
sections.summary: The relief is limited to specified contracts only, and security agencies providing security services at buildings are not covered under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, I note that this relief is limited to certain specified contracts only.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I have received feedback from one type of business which has not been covered under the Bill – security agencies which provide security services at various buildings in Singapore.

sections.label: Extend relief to security agencies
sections.summary: The Minister is urged to extend protection and relief under the Bill to security agencies so they have respite from legal action by service buyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Security agencies perform a very important service in ensuring safety for the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge the Minister to extend protection and relief under the Bill to security agencies, so that they have a respite from legal action by service buyers during this difficult period.

sections.label: Measures temporary for six months
sections.summary: The measures are temporary and will be in place for only six months at the first instance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In this respect, I am heartened to note that these measures are temporary and will be in place for only six months at the first instance.

sections.label: Union alternative arrangements guidelines
sections.summary: The Minister could provide by Order that the Registrar of Trade Unions may issue guidelines on alternative arrangements unions may adopt, since electronic voting may not be feasible for secret ballots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, in the case of matters which need to be decided by a secret ballot, it would not be feasible to allow voting to be done by electronic means at a meeting, as the unions may or may not have systems which provide the levels of security and confidentiality which the Registrar of Trade Unions may mandated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to propose that where unions are concerned, the Minister could provide by Order that the Registrar of Trade Unions, as the regulatory authority, may come up with guidelines relating to alternative arrangements which unions may adopt.

sections.label: Remote proceedings for overseas witnesses
sections.summary: Clause 28 expands the current position by allowing overseas witnesses to appear by remote proceedings in criminal proceedings if the parties consent, given fairness to the parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: To sum up, the extraordinary nature of this Bill amidst these extraordinary times call for extraordinary understanding and appreciation by parties, litigants, the legal and judicial system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Under clause 28, it is an enabling provision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, the current position under the Evidence Act is that in all non-criminal proceedings, the Court may permit any witness to give evidence by video or television link in remote proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This is for all types of witnesses, whether expert or factual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But in criminal proceedings, the current position is that all witnesses must be present in Singapore and the current position is therefore narrower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: What the Bill does, is to try to expand this slightly given the current situation by allowing overseas witnesses to appear by remote proceedings if the parties consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And the reason for this is because, in criminal proceedings, life and liberty is at stake and we want to ensure that the overriding consideration is fairness to the parties.

sections.label: Passing on benefits milestones
sections.summary: Property owners must pass on benefits they received at two milestones, by July 2020 and December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The property owners will be required to pass on the benefits they received at two milestones, namely by July 2020 and December 2020.

sections.label: Maximum fine and property tax accounts
sections.summary: The $5,000 maximum fine is compounded up to $5,000 per property tax account for non-compliant owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Fourth, on the maximum fine of $5,000 and whether or not that is sufficient as a deterrent against non-compliant property owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Second, remember that property tax is paid on a per account basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, a retail mall, for example, would have multiple property tax accounts to pay and if they were to not comply with multiple property tax accounts, then the fine of $5,000 will be compounded up to $5,000 per account.

sections.label: Tenants' civil action for rebate
sections.summary: Tenants can bring civil action against a property owner to enforce passing down the property tax rebate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Tenants can bring civil action against a property owner to enforce the obligation to pass down the property tax rebate.

sections.label: COVID-19 Bill and specific contracts
sections.summary: The COVID-19 Bill is not a general intervention to all contracts; NTUC is suggested to study two contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The general point I want to make is that this COVID-19 Bill is not intended to be a general intervention to all contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Both Mr Zainal and Mr Tay are Labour Movement Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I suggest that NTUC study these two contracts that they have specifically talked about, whether they think that a case can be made out – that COVID-19 has particularly affected these contracts and some relief ought to be given, because performance has been affected by COVID-19 in an unexpected way and it is unfair to expect performance.

sections.label: Bill covers forfeited deposits
sections.summary: The Bill covers deposits which may have been forfeited.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, deposits which may have been forfeited.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Now, the Bill covers deposits which may have been forfeited.

sections.label: Postponing booked events
sections.summary: The fairest rule is to postpone a booked event or venue if it cannot be held because of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One possibility, which I think is the fairest, is that as a rule, if you have booked an event or a certain venue, if now you cannot hold it because of COVID-19, the fairest is to postpone, if that is possible.

sections.label: Travel agency tour contracts
sections.summary: The contract for tours with travel agencies will be covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The contract for tours with travel agencies will be covered.

sections.label: Contracts after 25 March 2020
sections.summary: The Bill does not cover contracts entered into on or after 25 March 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Bill does not cover contracts entered into on or after 25 March 2020.

sections.label: Clause 5 relief for parties
sections.summary: Clause 5 relief applies to either contracting party unable to fulfill obligations and revise them fairly for both parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The relief under clause 5 of the Bill would apply to either contracting party which is unable to fulfill obligations and revise them in a way that seeks to be fair to both parties.

sections.label: Assessor determines tenant rent payment
sections.summary: If the Assessor finds the tenant can pay rent, he may determine payment in part or full immediately or after a prescribed period.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If the Assessor finds that the tenant is able to pay all or part of the rent, he may determine that the tenant pays that part or in full either immediately or after the expiry of a prescribed period.

sections.label: Tenant permission for three months
sections.summary: If the tenant seeks that permission, they will be given it for three months and then the Assessor can look at it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If the tenant seeks that permission, they will be given that for three months and then the Assessor can look at it.

sections.label: Six-month cash flow relief
sections.summary: The focus is immediate cash flow relief by suspending for six months, with relief for months determined by the Assessor.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: At this stage, we are focusing on immediate cash flow relief by suspending for a period of six months, or rather, the Bill is for six months; relief is for a period of months, as determined by the Assessor.

sections.label: Landlord set-off against security deposit
sections.summary: The passage states nothing prevents a landlord from setting off against the security deposit, and it need not go to the Assessor.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It does not even need to go to the Assessor.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have already said there is nothing to prevent set-off by the landlord against the security deposit.

sections.label: Assessors weigh landlord's tenant queue
sections.summary: Assessors will take into account a landlord's showing that tenants are queuing and it is unfair to let a tenant continue without paying rental.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If the landlord can show that, yes, there is a queue of tenants waiting to come in and it is unfair to the landlord to allow a particular tenant to carry on without paying rental, that is something the Assessors will take into account.

sections.label: HDB renovation permits during circuit breaker
sections.summary: From 7 April to 4 May 2020 HDB will not issue new renovation permits but will allow ongoing works and minimal essential works to be completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If you are not able to perform, if the law requires you to be in a certain situation, there is nothing you can do.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And I am given to understand that during this period, 7 April to 4 May 2020, HDB will also not issue any new renovation permits, but HDB will allow on-going renovation works to be completed if it would take only a few days to complete essential works.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Basically, if you can do the work within two or three days, and it can be safe for residents to stay, HDB will allow you to do it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For those with no other housing options in this situation, HDB will be prepared to allow a few more days to complete minimal essential works to make the place liveable in the interim.

sections.label: No cap on Assessor claims
sections.summary: Several Members asked questions on Assessors, and there is no minimum or maximum cap on the value of claims brought to the Assessors.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi, Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr de Souza had a number of questions on Assessors.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There is no minimum or maximum cap on the value of the claims that may be brought to the Assessors.

sections.label: COVID-19 as material reason
sections.summary: COVID-19 need not be the dominant cause but cannot be remote or insignificant, and the notification for relief must be served to rely on clause 6.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It need not be the dominant cause but it cannot be a remote, insignificant cause either.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It can cover situations where there is more than one reason for the inability to perform the obligation as long as COVID-19 is a material reason.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The notification for relief has to be served in order for the contractor to rely on clause 6.

sections.label: Three-month period then review
sections.summary: The general position is three months then review, and hire-purchase vehicles not used purely for business were left out.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I should correct this: they may review it depending on what the first order is.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It does not preclude giving a longer period or shorter period, but the general position would be three months and then review.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng specifically mentioned the case of a lady who had a car hire-purchase and she uses it for purposes of her work.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We gave some thought to it when we considered it and we left it out, when you take a hire-purchase vehicle and it is not used purely for business.

sections.label: Arbitration Act and trading contracts
sections.summary: Speaker says he did not raise trading contracts in his speech and asks about the Arbitration Act reference in clause 5(3)(b).

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Neither to my recollection, did I raise the issue about trading contracts in my delivered speech so I will let the record speak for itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I have a short clarification to ask in relation to the hon Minister's response to the reference to the Arbitration Act in clause 5(3)(b) of the Bill, Minister mentioned that this was looked at very carefully and what he does not want to do is to affect international arbitration.

sections.label: International arbitration reputation concerns
sections.summary: Minister says he will study the matter carefully to avoid affecting Singapore's International Arbitration Centre reputation, weighing contracts and benefits against reputational damage.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I want to be very careful about this.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will study it, but given how much effort we have put into making Singapore an International Arbitration Centre, I want to be very careful about doing anything that potentially affects that perception.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We must also look at how many contracts fall in this category that he mentioned – international party and a Singapore party, arbitration in Singapore, coming out of the International Arbitration Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If it is not that many contracts – my understanding is it may not be that many – then I think we need to analyse it as a balance of benefits and the damage that could be done to our reputation through perception.      .

sections.label: Deposit refund options for events
sections.summary: Passage lists options when companies cannot immediately refund deposits: postponing the event, cancelling with full or partial repayment, or allowing time to repay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If we ask all companies to immediately refund there could also be serious trouble.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, in such situations, there are different solutions possible: (a) to postpone the event, and the deposit is held back; (b) cancel the event, and the deposit is repaid in full or partially, depending on expenses incurred, work done; and (c) if the deposit is to be repaid in part or in full and if the company needs time to repay the deposit, the Assessor will have to consider and decide if time needs to be given.

sections.label: Finance company re-possession and hire-purchase
sections.summary: Finance companies can state re-possession reasons to the Assessor, who decides justly; hire-purchase motor vehicle agreements were about $2 billion at end-2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If the finance company, on the other hand, is of the view that it has reasons to justify re-possession, it can state its position to the Assessor and the Assessor will consider the positions held by both sides and make a determination that is just and equitable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It is estimated that the value of hire-purchase agreements in respect of motor vehicles at the end of 2019 could be about $2 billion.

sections.label: SME loans outstanding value
sections.summary: The total value of loans outstanding to SMEs that might fall into this category is estimated at about $76 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: An estimate of the total value of loans outstanding to SMEs which might fall into this category is at about $76 billion.

sections.label: Panels, judges and assessors
sections.summary: There will be 12 panels each headed by a State Court Judge, and 100 or more Assessors are expected to be appointed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There will be 12 panels, each headed by a State Court Judge.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And we expect to appoint 100, maybe more, Assessors.

sections.label: Bankruptcy debt thresholds and timelines
sections.summary: For individuals, the debt repayment scheme rises to $250,000, bankruptcy applications require $100,000 owed, and the wait becomes six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: First, for individuals under the Bankruptcy Act, we are going to increase the debt repayment scheme to cover up to $250,000, as opposed to $100,000 in the past.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Second, in order to make a bankruptcy application, the amount owed must be a minimum of $100,000, instead of $10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: You have got to serve a statutory demand and you have got to wait for a number of days before you can serve a bankruptcy notice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We are going to make it six months.

sections.label: Company bankruptcy minimum and demand period
sections.summary: A company needs a minimum $100,000 debt to be made bankrupt, and the period from service of a demand increases from 21 days to six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: A company cannot be made a bankrupt unless it owes a minimum $100,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And likewise, we are also going to increase the number of days from service of a demand, from 21 days to six months.
